families.uncertainty: Atlassian publishes no token grammar. Its docs call the length 'varied', and its staff said in 2022 that tokens are opaque, then in 2025 that the ATAT prefix can be relied on. The 12-character ATATT3xFfGF0 header, the 192-character length and the =<8 uppercase hex> CRC32 suffix are empirical: one maintainer-issued key, a five-key report and scanner samples. The maintainer could not confirm the CRC32 on an issued key.
supportedContexts: bare ATAT... token anywhere on a line, quoted or unquoted
env/YAML/JSON/compose assignment (JIRA_API_TOKEN=..., settings.json, Pipelines variable)
CLI argument or curl -u email:token Basic auth
client-library config, debug log line, pasted ticket text

corroboration.supports: atlassian-api-token rule (L181-184): \bATATT3 + exactly 186 [A-Za-z0-9_\-=] (192 total); ATAT prefix, base64url body with '='
jiratoken v2 detector (L37-38, 'tokens created after Jan 18 2023 use a variable length'): ATATT + body + '=' + 8 alnum; the ATAT prefix and '=' suffix separator (not the ATCT 'atlassian' detector)
'Atlassian Cloud API Token' rule: ATATT3xFfGF0 + 20-200 [A-Za-z0-9_-] + '=' + [0-9A-F]{8}; the optional =<8 uppercase hex> suffix
ATATT3xFfGF0 + 80-800 [0-9A-Za-z_-] + '=' (or %3D) + [A-F0-9]{8}; its value_atlassian_token_check.py filter at the same tag checks the suffix as CRC32 of the preceding bytes
AtlassianTokenChecksum: trailing 8 hex = big-endian CRC32 over everything before them, '=' included; body alphabet [A-Za-z0-9_=-]
answer from an 'Atlassian Team' account (2025-08-25) on Atlassian's community site: 'You can rely on' API token prefix ATAT (ATBB, ATCT are other kinds); prefix only
Bitbucket client picks Basic+email auth when the token has the ATATT3x prefix, Bearer for ATCTT3x; ATAT prefix as the API-token identifier
2026-09-22 second-pass, broad-discovery and web-search passes plus the maintainer's answers: 192 = 12 header + 171 body + '=' + 8 uppercase hex, CRC32 on real samples

contradictions.statement: An unaffiliated 2026 r/jira reply says 'Atlassian does not use prefixes for api keys'; another says the shared header is base64(email:token).
contradictions.bound: An Atlassian Team answer on Atlassian's own community site (2025-08-25) says the ATAT prefix can be relied on, and the maintainer-issued key and every sample carry it; the unaffiliated no-prefix claim is refuted, so the unprefixed near-miss follows the provider statement.

contradictions.statement: Atlassian staff (2022-10-13): API tokens are opaque and clients 'cannot depend on their size, structure, or format'; staff (2025-08-25): 'You can rely on' ATAT.
contradictions.bound: The 2022 post predates the 2023-01-18 format change, when tokens were 24-char unprefixed. That generation is deliberately excluded (all expired by 2026-05-12 per Atlassian's support page) and no fixture uses a 24-char unprefixed value. For the current generation the provider's later staff statement names ATAT.

contradictions.statement: Length: support docs say 'varied' and staff say 'no specified range', but every observed token is 192. Other reports: 108-char exception tokens (ID-8131, expired), one unsupported 193-char claim (2023). gitleaks hard-codes 186 after ATATT3.
contradictions.bound: The contract keeps a 100-character body floor with no maximum, so it admits 108, 192 and 193. The only length twins sit below the floor (99-char body), and no source reports a token that short.

contradictions.statement: Header length: staff give ATAT (4); tools use ATATT (5), ATATT3 (6) or ATATT3xFfGF0 (12).
contradictions.bound: The contract anchors only the staff-confirmed ATAT. No fixture asserts on the 5th-12th characters (the prefix twin mutates to ATAQ, which no source names).

contradictions.statement: Suffix: Nosey Parker, CredSweeper and all samples use '=' + uppercase hex; TruffleHog accepts [A-Za-z0-9]{8}, DataDog also decodes lowercase hex, and gitleaks allows '=' anywhere in the body.
contradictions.bound: The contract admits only the optional =[0-9A-F]{8} suffix. No fixture uses a lowercase or non-hex suffix or a mid-body '='.

contradictions.statement: TruffleHog's jiratoken v2 body admits '+' and '/'; no observed sample contains either. CredSweeper also matches a URL-escaped %3D in place of '='.
contradictions.bound: Excluded by the contract's [A-Za-z0-9_-] body. The alphabet twin uses '!', and no fixture uses '+', '/' or %3D.

Segment 1 width follows from base64 of an 18- or 19-digit ID, which is arithmetic, not a stated rule. Discord gives no stability guarantee, and a maintainer-issued token has not been measured here.

contradictions.statement: Segment 1 width: 24 (18-digit ids; TruffleHog, lantern) vs 26 (19-digit ids since 2022-07-22); 23 for 17-digit pre-Oct-2015 ids.

contradictions.statement: Segment 2 as {6,7} (Sapphire utilities, no stated reason) vs 6 in every measured sample.

contradictions.bound: Single unverified outliers the contract excludes. No fixture uses a 40-char segment 3.

contradictions.statement: Leading character [MNO] (detect-secrets, several tools) vs 'no prefix' (GitGuardian lists the detector as 'Prefixed: True' without saying what).

contradictions.statement: Opacity: a 2026 issue on Discord's docs repo (#8091) asks that tokens be treated as opaque, and a Discord.Net maintainer (2018) says Discord gives no guarantee the length stays in range.
contradictions.bound: Not a competing shape. It is carried in `uncertainty`, since the frozen widths could change. No Discord statement either way.

families.uncertainty: Google never documented this shape, and its only published legacy server-key example is the older AIza form. Late-2016 keys have 162-183-char bodies. The legacy FCM API was shut down in June 2024, so no new key can be issued to check.

contradictions.statement: Body length: tools say exactly 140, but Firebase's Jan 2017 blog says 'a giant 175-character string', and late-2016 keys measure 162, 167 and 183 (8 of 66 real keys).
contradictions.bound: The contract deliberately freezes the dominant 2017+ generation (140). Its length twins use 139, which no source reports, and per FIELDS_207 no fixture asserts silence on 162/167/183.

contradictions.statement: Google's only published legacy server-key example (auth-server snapshots 2016-2024, GCM docs) is AIza-shaped, not AAAA...:....
contradictions.bound: That is the older key relabelled 'Legacy server key' in 2016, a Google API key (covered by google-api-key). This contract covers only the newer AAAA...:... key, and no firebase-server-key fixture uses an AIza value.

contradictions.statement: AAAA is not a designed marker: the 11-char head is the base64url of the project number, so a project number >= 2^40 would give an AAAB... head. The largest observed is within 2.1% of that bound.
contradictions.bound: The contract requires AAAA; no key can be issued since June 2024 and none above 2^40 was observed. The only non-AAAA near-miss uses a 'Qo' head, which decodes to about 2^62, far outside any project-number range, so no fixture asserts on the plausible AAAB-AAAP range.

contradictions.statement: Firebase's 2017 blog screenshot shows a mocked server key with a 10-char head and no AAAA.
contradictions.bound: A fabricated screenshot value; every real sample has an 11-char AAAA head. The long-head twin (12 chars) is a width no source reports.

contradictions.statement: Every real key's body starts APA91b (pleno-dlp and ~20 scanners pin it); the 140-regex tools and synthetic fixtures do not.
contradictions.bound: The contract does not require APA91b and no fixture asserts silence on a non-APA91b body; positives carry it.

contradictions.statement: 'Legacy' names different keys across eras (the AIza key in 2016-2018 consoles; the whole AAAA key after the 2023-2024 legacy-API deprecation).
